title: Mario Party 5
subtitle: A party inside the Dream Depot
summary: Mario Party 5 is Hudson Soft's second GameCube party game, first released in North America on 11 November 2003.
body: Mario Party 5 is Hudson Soft's second GameCube party game, first released in North America on 11 November 2003. The Dream Depot provides a set of fantastical boards where Mario and the other players compete for Stars. Coins earned through movement and minigames help shape that contest, while a single-player story pits the chosen character against Bowser's Koopa Kids. The setting gives each board another playful theme, but the larger rhythm remains a gathering repeatedly interrupted by small tests of reactions, cooperation and luck.

Capsules introduce a different item system. They can affect a player directly or be placed on board spaces, leaving an effect for whoever later reaches them. Extra movement, stolen coins and other changes make the route a place the competitors can modify as well as traverse. A player must consider both the immediate benefit of an item and what it might do to someone else's next turn. Minigames continue to replenish the coins that keep those small acts of interference possible.

Super Duel adds a separate activity in which players assemble battle vehicles from parts and fight other machines. It extends the competitive gathering beyond the boards, offering a more direct contest around a personally built vehicle. Toad, Boo and Koopa Kid join the playable roster, and Aya Tanaka composed the music. Mario Party 5 uses the Dream Depot's variety to connect several scales of competition: a whole board match, a minigame lasting moments and a vehicle battle whose outcome depends on the machine brought into it.
